en: The Philippines actually consists of 7,641 islands, a number updated after a 2016 national mapping project discovered new landmasses.
Mount Apo is the highest mountain in the Philippines, standing at 2,954 meters above sea level in Mindanao.
The Cagayan River is the longest river in the Philippines, stretching approximately 505 kilometers through the Cagayan Valley.
Laguna de Bay is the largest lake in the Philippines, covering an area of about 911 square kilometers across Laguna and Rizal.
Taal Volcano is a complex system featuring a main crater lake that holds its own island, Vulcan Point.
Mayon Volcano is the most active volcano in the Philippines, having erupted over 50 times in the last 400 years.
The critically endangered Philippine eagle primarily inhabits the dense tropical forests of Mindanao and parts of Leyte, not Luzon.
The Philippines experiences four main climate types under the Corona classification, meaning not all regions share the exact same wet and dry seasons.
The Cordillera Administrative Region is a geographical region composed of six distinct provinces, not a single province itself.
The West Philippine Sea is the official designation for only the eastern portions of the South China Sea within the Philippine exclusive economic zone.
The Chocolate Hills in Bohol were actually formed by the weathering and erosion of marine limestone, not by ancient volcanic eruptions.
The Banaue Rice Terraces were carved into the mountains by the indigenous Ifugao people over 2,000 years ago, long before Spanish colonization.
